title: Sales HackLab: Integrator Prototype Notes
content:
Context and intent:
- Lightweight experiment to produce a 6-slide micro-deck + one-page battlecard aimed specifically at integrator/platform engineering personas.
- Goal: cut friction in pilot conversations where buyer cares about latency cost tradeoffs, routing, and fallback strategies.
- Constraints: 2 engineers (SE + solution architect) can present in 5 minutes. Deck must be skimmable and have a concrete call-to-action (pilot checklist + short canary).

What we built (proto):
- 6 slides (title, problem, how Redwood fits, evidence, canary checklist, next steps).
- Single-side PDF battlecard with: 3 signals for risk, 3 fallback scripts, 2 quick SLO commitments, and an API/infra footprint snippet.

Slide-by-slide sketch (raw):
1) Title: "Integrating Inference: predictable latency, cost, and fallbacks"
   - 1-line positioning, 10s hook: "Serve at 99th percentile latency, keep cost under $X/token with caching+quant profiles."
2) Problem: "Why integrators pause"
   - bullet: ambiguous throughput, unknown tail latency, complex infra pivots
   - note: use a quick quote from an actual prospect (redacted) about 'surprise bursts'
3) Redwood map: "How we un-block infra teams"
   - small diagram: client -> routing -> dedicated/dynamic -> KV cache -> model variants
   - callout: private deploy compatibility, KMS, audit logs (one-liner each)
4) Evidence: "3 quick proof points"
   - 1) Bench: 2.4x throughput on opt-64 quantized baseline (internal test id: bench-2024-11)
   - 2) Canary story: auto-fallback kept service online during a region outage (customer X, anonymized)
   - 3) Cost delta example: typical chat endpoint reduced token-cost by 27% with routing + prefix cache
5) Canary checklist (for SE to run live):
   - prep: sandbox API key, sample prompt set (link), expected SLO numbers
   - steps: dry run w/ 100 reqs/min; enable canary routing to fallback variant; simulate 30s GPU OOM -> observe fallback behavior; monitor token-cost telemetry
   - metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model-change error rate
6) Next steps + CTA:
   - "Pilot in 2 weeks" timeline: 1) 1-hr kickoff, 2) 3-day smoke, 3) 2-week pilot with reserved capacity trial
   - contact: se@redwood-inference.com, playbook link (internal)

Battlecard (one-pager) draft (bullets / skimmable):
- Audience: Integration Architect / Platform Engineer
- Top 3 buyer concerns and suggested scripts:
  1) Concern: "How do you avoid tail latency spikes?"
     - Script: "We use workload-aware batching, continuous KV prefix caching, and priority routing. If usage spikes, canary routing falls back to a compatible model with identical API semantics while preserving SLA."
  2) Concern: "How do we control costs when usage is highly variable?"
     - Script: "We recommend dedicated pools + burst cap for steady load, and autoscale with pre-warmed instances for spiky loads; plus recommended quantization profiles for non-critical endpoints."
  3) Concern: "What happens when a GPU node OOMs or a kernel fails?"
     - Script: "Automatic health checks trigger routing to the next tier; we maintain KV cache compatibility across model variants to reduce cold-start cost and latency."
- Quick technical data:
  - Example footprint: ~1 p95 response (512 tokens) -> baseline: 220ms hosted; dedicated configured: 120ms median, 200ms p95 (numbers illustrative).
  - Telemetry pointers: token-cost per route, per-token breakdown by stage (queue, compute, network).
- Red team: top 2 risks and mitigation:
  - Risk: Model-quality regression during fallback -> Mitigate: evaluate a small fuzz-prompt set in canary, automated rollback rule if regression > threshold
  - Risk: Unexpected egress/policy objections -> Mitigate: private deploy option + audit log sample export

Experiment notes / findings from first pilots (raw):
- Pilot A (fintech integrator): friction at procurement around reserved v burst pricing. Quick win: showed 3-month cost projection with and without prefix cache -> accelerated procurement.
- Pilot B (healthcare): needed HSM integration. Private deploy + KMS slide closed meeting.
- SE feedback: bring a one-line 'what I need from you' for engineering leads (e.g., sample traffic pattern, spike window, compliance checklist).

Open questions / next iterations:
- Should we include a tiny code snippet showing fallback in the SDK? (yes if time permits)
- Add a mini-diagram for caching lifetime and KV TTL behavior (engineers asked for this explicitly)
- Simplify canary checklist into a checkbox form for SE to hand over to the customer post-demo

Notes to self (choppy):
- remove any phrase "best-in-class" from slides -> sounds marketingy
- add one line about SLA commitments (what we can sign vs what is approximate)
- map the bench numbers to an internal repo id before sharing externally

Action items (short):
- Ethan: make a 1-slide code snippet showing SDK fallback by 2025-01-10
- Samira: produce the single-page battlecard PDF template and run A/B copy test in next SE dry-run (due 2025-01-15)
- Marco: grab bench numbers and redact customer IDs (due 2025-01-12)
- Priya (owner): run a 15-min lightning dry-run with SEs on 2025-01-20 and collect five quick improvement notes

Attachments / artifacts to link later:
- internal playbook draft (confluence://playbooks/inference-integrator-onramp)
